metadata.title: A local lemma via entropy compression
metadata.authors: Rogerio G. Alves, Aldo Procacci, Remy Sanchis

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma (lopsided version)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{F}$ be a finite collection of events with graph $\mathcal{G}$ on $\mathfrak{F}$. If $\mathrm{P}(\mathfrak{e}|\bigcap_{\mathfrak{e}'\in U}\bar{\mathfrak{e}'}) \leq \mu_\mathfrak{e}/\Phi_\mathfrak{e}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\mathcal{G})$ with $\Phi_\mathfrak{e}=\prod_{\mathfrak{e}'\in\Gamma_\mathcal{G}(\mathfrak{e})}(1+\mu_{\mathfrak{e}'})$, then $\mathrm{P}(\bigcap_{\mathfrak{e}}\bar{\mathfrak{e}})>0$.
assumptions: $\mathfrak{F}$ is a finite collection of events in $(\Omega,\mathrm{P})$
$\mathcal{G}$ is a graph with vertex set $\mathfrak{F}$
nodes.origin_citation: Erdos & Lovasz 1975; lopsided version: Scott & Sokal 2005

nodes.name: Cluster Expansion Local Lemma (CELL)
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem $\ref{lov}$, if $\mathrm{P}(\mathfrak{e}|\bigcap_{\mathfrak{e}'\in U}\bar{\mathfrak{e}'})\leq\mu_\mathfrak{e}/\Xi_\mathfrak{e}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\mathcal{G})$ with $\Xi_\mathfrak{e}=\sum_{Y\subseteq\Gamma_\mathcal{G}(\mathfrak{e}),Y\text{ indep}}\prod_{\mathfrak{e}'\in Y}\mu_{\mathfrak{e}'}$, then $\mathrm{P}(\bigcap_\mathfrak{e}\bar{\mathfrak{e}})>0$.

nodes.name: Algorithmic CELL (Pegden's extension of Moser-Tardos)
nodes.statement: Given $\mathbf{S}$ with i.i.d. random variables $\psi_\mathbf{S}$, family $\mathcal{O}$ of subsets of $\mathbf{S}$, and bad events $\mathfrak{F}$: if the cluster expansion criterion holds, then $\bigcap_{\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}}\bar{\mathfrak{e}}\neq\emptyset$ and the MT-algorithm finds $\omega\in\bigcap\bar{\mathfrak{e}}$ in expected steps $\leq\sum_\mathfrak{e}\mu_\mathfrak{e}$.
assumptions: Finite set $\mathbf{S}$ with mutually independent random variables $\psi_\mathbf{S}$
$\mathcal{O}$ collection of subsets of $\mathbf{S}$ and $\mathfrak{F}$ family of bad events with natural dependency graph $\mathcal{G}$
Cluster expansion criterion (\ref{cond1n}) holds for each $\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}$

nodes.name: MT-Algorithm (Moser-Tardos)
nodes.statement: Random resampling algorithm: at each step, if the current configuration $\omega_{i-1}$ violates some bad event $\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}$, resample the variables in $\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})$ uniformly.
input: Finite set $\mathbf{S}$ with mutually independent random variables $\{\psi_x\}_{x\in\mathbf{S}}$
Family $\mathcal{O}$ of subsets of $\mathbf{S}$ and family $\mathfrak{F}$ of bad events
output: Configuration $\omega\in\Psi_\mathbf{S}$ such that no event in $\mathfrak{F}$ occurs

nodes.name: Variable setting (Moser-Tardos)
nodes.statement: Probability space $(\Omega_\mathbf{S},\mathrm{P}_\mathbf{S})$ generated by a finite collection $\{\psi_x\}_{x\in\mathbf{S}}$ of mutually independent random variables, with $\psi_x$ taking values in $\Psi_x$. Each event $\mathfrak{e}$ is associated to an object $A=\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\in\mathcal{O}\subset 2^\mathbf{S}$.

nodes.name: Natural dependency graph
nodes.statement: The graph $\mathcal{G}$ with vertex set $\mathfrak{F}$ and edges $\{\mathfrak{e},\mathfrak{e}'\}$ whenever $\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\cap\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e}')\neq\emptyset$. Two events with disjoint objects are necessarily independent.

nodes.name: Symmetric LLL criterion
nodes.statement: $ep(d+1)\leq 1$, where $d=\max_{\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}}|\Gamma^*_\mathcal{G}(\mathfrak{e})|$ and $p$ is a uniform upper bound on conditional probabilities of bad events.

nodes.name: Clique estimate of $\Xi_\mathfrak{e}$
nodes.statement: $\Xi_\mathfrak{e}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\mathcal{G})\leq\Xi^{\mathrm{clique}}_\mathfrak{e}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\mathcal{G})\equiv\prod_{y\in\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})}[1+\sum_{\mathfrak{e}'\in\mathfrak{F}(y)}\mu_{\mathfrak{e}'}]$.

nodes.name: EC-setting (atoms, colors, objects, flaws)
nodes.statement: Pair $(\mathbf{S},k)$ with $\mathbf{S}$ finite (atoms), $[k]$ colors. A coloring is $\kappa:\mathbf{S}\to[k]$, partial coloring $\gamma:\mathbf{S}\to[k]_0=[k]\cup\{0\}$. For $\mathcal{O}\subset 2^\mathbf{S}$ (objects) and $A\in\mathcal{O}$, a standard flaw is $\mathfrak{e}\subset[k]^A$; non-standard flaw is $\mathfrak{f}:[k]_0^{\mathbf{S}\setminus A}\to\mathcal{P}([k]^A)$.

nodes.name: Tidy flaw and seed
nodes.statement: A flaw $\mathfrak{e}$ is tidy if for all $y\in\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})$ there exists $X\subset\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\setminus\{y\}$ such that any coloring $\kappa\in\mathfrak{e}$ is uniquely determined by its restriction to $X$, and $X$ is minimal with this property. The set $X$ is called a seed of $\mathfrak{e}$.

nodes.name: Power (effective size) of an event
nodes.statement: For $\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}(y)$, $\kappa_y(\mathfrak{e})=\min\{|X|:X\subset\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\setminus\{y\},X\text{ is a seed of }\mathfrak{e}\}$ and $\|\mathfrak{e}_y\|=|\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})|-\kappa_y(\mathfrak{e})$ is the power of $\mathfrak{e}$ w.r.t. $y$.

nodes.name: Exponent set $E_\mathcal{O}$ and generating function $\phi_\mathcal{O}$
nodes.statement: $E_\mathcal{O}=\{j\in\mathbb{N}:\exists y\in\mathbf{S}, \mathfrak{F}_j(y)\neq\emptyset\}$ where $\mathfrak{F}_j(y)=\{\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}(y):\|\mathfrak{e}_y\|=j\}$ and $d_j=\max_{y,\gamma}|\mathfrak{F}_j(y)|$. The function $\phi_\mathcal{O}(x)=1+\sum_{j\in E_\mathcal{O}}d_j x^j$.

nodes.name: EC-Algorithm
nodes.statement: Iterative random coloring algorithm: at each step, color the smallest uncolored atom $y$ using the next entry of input vector $F_t$; if a flaw occurs, partially uncolor by selecting the smallest occurring flaw and discoloring all atoms in $\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\setminus G(\mathfrak{e},y)$.
input: Pair $(\mathbf{S},k)$ with family of objects $\mathcal{O}$ and family $\mathfrak{F}$ of flaws associated to $\mathcal{O}$
Vector $F_t\in[k]^t$ of length $t$ with entries in $[k]$ (deterministic) or sampled uniformly i.i.d. (random)
output: Partial coloring $\gamma_i$ that avoids all flaws in $\mathfrak{F}$

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.statement: Step 0: Set $\gamma_0\equiv 0$ (no atom is colored).

nodes.name: Main loop: pick smallest uncolored atom and color
nodes.statement: Step $i\geq 1$: if $\gamma_{i-1}^{-1}(0)\neq\emptyset$, let $y$ be the smallest uncolored atom, take entry $s\in[k]$ from $F_t$, and form $\gamma_{i-1}]^s_y$.

nodes.name: Branch on whether a flaw occurred
nodes.statement: If no flaw occurs given $\gamma_{i-1}]^s_y$, set $\gamma_i=\gamma_{i-1}]^s_y$. Otherwise select the smallest occurring flaw $\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}(y)$ and set $\gamma_i=\gamma_{i-1}]^0_{G^c(\mathfrak{e},y)}$ (uncolor all atoms in $\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\setminus G(\mathfrak{e},y)$).

nodes.name: Termination
nodes.statement: If $\gamma_{i-1}^{-1}(0)=\emptyset$, stop and discard remaining entries $f_i,\dots,f_t$ of $F_t$. Successful if stops with all atoms colored or completes $t$ steps with $\gamma_t^{-1}(0)=\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Entropy-Compression Lemma
nodes.statement: If $k>\inf_{x>0}\phi_\mathcal{O}(x)/x$, then $\bigcap_{\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}_\mathcal{O}}\bar{\mathfrak{e}}\neq\emptyset$. Moreover, if the inequality holds strictly, the random EC-algorithm finds a coloring $c\in\bigcap\bar{\mathfrak{e}}$ in expected number of steps linear in $|\mathbf{S}|$.
assumptions: Family $\mathcal{O}$ of objects (subsets of $\mathbf{S}$) and family $\mathfrak{F}$ of (tidy) flaws associated to $\mathcal{O}$
conclusions: If $k>\inf_{x>0}\phi_\mathcal{O}(x)/x$, the random EC-algorithm finds $c\in\bigcap\bar{\mathfrak{e}}$ in expected steps linear in $|\mathbf{S}|$

nodes.name: Proof of Entropy-Compression Lemma (Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: Bound $|\mathcal{F}_t|$ (set of failure inputs) via injective record map $\mathcal{M}:F_t\mapsto(R_t,\gamma_t)$, encode records as partial Dyck words and rooted plane trees, then apply Drmota's analytic-combinatorics asymptotic to conclude $|\mathcal{F}_t|<k^t$ when $k\geq\inf_{x>0}\phi_\mathcal{O}(x)/x$.

nodes.name: Define record map $\mathcal{M}$
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{F}_t\subset[k]^t$ as the failure set (vectors $F_t$ for which the algorithm fails). For $F_t\in\mathcal{F}_t$, define record $(R_t,\gamma_t)$ where $R_t=r_1\cdots r_t$ has $r_i=0$ if no flaw at step $i$ or $r_i=(j,\ell)$ if flaw $\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}_j(y)$ identified by $(j,\ell)\in E_\mathcal{O}\times[d_j]$.

nodes.name: Set of uncolored atoms determined by record
nodes.statement: The set $X_t=\gamma_t^{-1}(0)$ of uncolored atoms at step $t$ is uniquely determined by the string $R_t$.
assumptions: Family $\mathfrak{F}$ of tidy flaws associated to $\mathcal{O}$
conclusions: $X_t=\gamma_t^{-1}(0)$ is uniquely determined by the string $R_t$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Induction on $t$. Base case $t=1$: $X_1$ is determined by $R_1$. Inductive step: by IH $X_{t-1}$ is determined by $R_{t-1}$; if $r_t=0$ then $X_t=X_{t-1}\setminus\{y\}$; if $r_t=(j,\ell)$ then $X_t=X_{t-1}\setminus(\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\setminus G(\mathfrak{e},y))$.

nodes.name: Base case $t=1$
nodes.statement: If $R_1=0$ the first atom $x$ stays colored, so $X_1=\mathbf{S}\setminus\{x\}$. If $R_1\neq 0$ then a flaw occurs (necessarily elementary, effective size 1) and $x$ is uncolored, so $X_1=\mathbf{S}$.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: By IH $X_{t-1}$ is determined by $R_{t-1}$; the smallest atom $y\in X_{t-1}$ is colored at step $t$. If $r_t=0$, $X_t=X_{t-1}\setminus\{y\}$. If $r_t=(j,\ell)$, the flaw $\mathfrak{e}$ is uniquely determined and $X_t=X_{t-1}\setminus(\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})\setminus G(\mathfrak{e},y))$.

nodes.name: Injectivity of record map
nodes.statement: For any $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the map $\mathcal{M}:\mathcal{F}_t\to(R_t,\gamma_t)$ is injective.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2 (injectivity)
nodes.statement: Induction on $t$ reconstructing $F_t$ from the record. Use Lemma 3.1 to identify the smallest uncolored atom $y$, then split into cases $r_t=0$ vs $r_t=(j,\ell)$ to recover $f_t$ and $\gamma_{t-1}$. The seed property of $G(\mathfrak{e},y)$ recovers the discarded colors.

nodes.name: Base case $t=1$
nodes.statement: If $r_1=0$, $\gamma_1(x)=s$ recovers $f_1=s$. If $r_1=(1,\ell)$, the elementary flaw $\mathfrak{e}$ identifies the $\ell$-th forbidden color, recovering $f_1$.

nodes.name: Inductive step: case $r_t=0$
nodes.statement: If $r_t=0$, then $f_t=\gamma_t(y)=s$ and $\gamma_{t-1}$ agrees with $\gamma_t$ outside $\{y\}$ with $\gamma_{t-1}(y)=0$.

nodes.name: Inductive step: case $r_t=(j,\ell)$
nodes.statement: If $r_t=(j,\ell)$, the flaw $\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}_j(y)$ is identified. Since $G(\mathfrak{e},y)$ is a seed and $\gamma_t$ is known, the colors of atoms in $G^c(\mathfrak{e},y)$ are recovered. Then $f_t=c(y)\in[k]$.

nodes.name: Cardinality bound for failure set
nodes.statement: $|\mathcal{F}_t|\leq(k+1)^{|\mathbf{S}|}\sum_{r=1}^{|\mathbf{S}|}|\mathcal{R}^r_t|$, where $\mathcal{R}^r_t$ is the set of records arising from $\mathcal{F}^r_t$ (failure inputs leaving exactly $r$ uncolored atoms).

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: By Lemma 3.2 (injectivity), $|\mathcal{F}^r_t|\leq|\mathcal{R}^r_t||\mathcal{G}^r_t|\leq|\mathcal{R}^r_t|(k+1)^{|\mathbf{S}|}$. Summing over $r$ yields the bound.

nodes.name: (Partial) Dyck word and ${\cal D}_{n,r,E}$
nodes.statement: A partial Dyck word is a $\{0,1\}$-word in which every initial segment has at least as many 0's as 1's; a Dyck word equalizes them. ${\cal D}_{n,r,E}$ denotes the set of partial Dyck words with $n$ 0's, $n-r$ 1's and descents (maximal runs of 1's) of cardinality in $E$.

nodes.name: Bound on partial Dyck words via Dyck words
nodes.statement: Let $m_E=\min(E\setminus\{1\})$. Then $|{\cal D}_{n,r,E}|\leq|{\cal D}_{n+r(m_E-1),E}|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: Construct injection $f:{\cal D}_{n,r,E}\to{\cal D}_{n+r(m_E-1),E}$ by appending $(0^{m_E-1}1^{m_E})^r$ at the end of each partial Dyck word.

nodes.name: Bijection between rooted plane trees and Dyck words
nodes.statement: There is a bijection $h:\mathcal{T}_{n+1,E}\to{\cal D}_{n,E}$, $\tau\mapsto w$, such that for any $j\in E$, $\delta_j(\tau)=\delta_j(w)$ (where $\delta_j$ counts vertices with $j$ children / descents of size $j$).
assumptions: $\mathcal{T}_{n+1,E}$ is the set of plane rooted trees with $n+1$ vertices and number of children of each internal vertex in $E$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.4
nodes.statement: DFS traversal of $\tau$ gives a string $\rho_\tau=v_1\cdots v_n$; replace each $v_i$ by $0^{s_i}1$ where $s_i$ is the number of children of $v_i$. The composition $\tau\to u\to\widetilde{u}\to w$ (mirror image and 0-1 swap) is a bijection preserving descent statistics.

nodes.name: Record-to-Dyck-word map is well-defined
nodes.statement: For $R_t\in{\cal R}^r_t$, the word $R^*_t$ obtained by replacing each $r_i=(j,\ell)$ with $01^j$ is a partial Dyck word with $t$ 0's and $t-r$ 1's and descents in $E_\mathcal{O}$. Hence $R^*_t\in{\cal D}_{t,r,E_\mathcal{O}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: Each 0 in $R^*_t$ corresponds to a coloring step and each 1 to an uncoloring step; the number of 0's is $t$ and 1's is $t-r$. Cannot uncolor more than colored, so the word is a partial Dyck word; descents have size $j\in E_\mathcal{O}$ by construction.

nodes.name: Pre-image bound for record map
nodes.statement: $|\mathfrak{M}^{-1}(R^*_t)|\leq\prod_{j\in E_\mathcal{O}}(d_j)^{\delta_j(R^*_t)}$, where $\delta_j(R^*_t)$ is the number of descents of size $j$ in $R^*_t$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: Each descent of size $j$ corresponds to a flaw of size $j$ at a fixed atom; there are at most $d_j$ such flaws, giving the product bound.

nodes.name: Tree-sum bound for $|{\cal R}^r_t|$
nodes.statement: $|{\cal R}^r_t|\leq\sum_{\tau\in{\cal T}_{t+r(m_{E_\mathcal{O}}-1)+1}}\prod_{j\geq 0}\varphi_j^{\delta_j(\tau)}$, where $\varphi_0=1$, $\varphi_j=d_j$ for $j\in E_\mathcal{O}$, $\varphi_j=0$ otherwise.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: Combine Lemmas 3.5 and 3.6 to bound $|{\cal R}^r_t|$ by a sum over partial Dyck words; apply Lemma 3.3 to extend to Dyck words; apply Lemma 3.4 to convert the Dyck-word sum into a tree sum.

nodes.name: Apply Lemmas 3.5 and 3.6
nodes.statement: $|{\cal R}^r_t|\leq\sum_{w\in{\cal D}_{t,r,E_\mathcal{O}}}\prod_{j\in E_\mathcal{O}}(d_j)^{\delta_j(w)}$.

nodes.name: Embed partial Dyck words into Dyck words via Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: $\sum_{w\in{\cal D}_{t,r,E_\mathcal{O}}}\prod_j(d_j)^{\delta_j(w)}\leq\sum_{w\in{\cal D}_{t+r(m_{E_\mathcal{O}}-1),E_\mathcal{O}}}\prod_j(d_j)^{\delta_j(w)}$.

nodes.name: Apply tree-Dyck bijection (Lemma 3.4) and rewrite
nodes.statement: Convert the Dyck-word sum into a sum over rooted plane trees ${\cal T}_{t+r(m_{E_\mathcal{O}}-1)+1}$ using $\delta_j(\tau)=\delta_j(w)$ and the definition of $\varphi_j$.

nodes.name: Drmota's tree-sum asymptotic
nodes.statement: For $\{\varphi_j\}_{j\geq 0}$ nonneg., $\varphi(x)=\sum_j\varphi_j x^j$ with radius $R$ and $\xi$ first root in $[0,R)$ of $x\varphi'(x)-\varphi(x)=0$: $\sum_{\tau\in{\cal T}_n}\prod_j\varphi_j^{\delta_j(\tau)}\leq C_\varphi[\varphi'(\xi)]^n/n^{3/2}$. Also $\varphi'(\xi)=\min_{x>0}\varphi(x)/x$.
assumptions: $\xi$ is the first root of $x\varphi'(x)-\varphi(x)=0$ in $[0,R)$

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 3.1 to $|\mathcal{F}_t|$
nodes.statement: By Proposition 3.1, $|\mathcal{F}_t|\leq(k+1)^{|\mathbf{S}|}\sum_r|{\cal R}^r_t|$.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 3.2 + Drmota
nodes.statement: By Proposition 3.2 and Drmota's theorem with $\varphi=\phi_\mathcal{O}$, $|{\cal R}^r_t|\leq C_\varphi[\phi'_\mathcal{O}(\xi)]^{t+r(m_{E_\mathcal{O}}-1)+1}/(t+r(m_{E_\mathcal{O}}-1)+1)^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Bound $|\mathcal{F}_t|<k^t$
nodes.statement: Combine to get $|\mathcal{F}_t|\leq C_{\varphi,\mathbf{S},k}[\phi'_\mathcal{O}(\xi)]^t/t^{3/2}$. If $\phi'_\mathcal{O}(\xi)=\min_{x>0}\phi_\mathcal{O}(x)/x\leq k$, then $|\mathcal{F}_t|<k^t$ for $t$ large enough, so the algorithm terminates.

nodes.name: Bound expected running time (strict inequality)
nodes.statement: If $\phi'_\mathcal{O}(\xi)\leq(1-\varepsilon)k$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, then $P(t_0+t)\leq(1-\varepsilon)^t=e^{-t|\ln(1-\varepsilon)|}$ with $t_0$ linear in $|\mathbf{S}|$, so expected running time $T\leq t_0+1/|\ln(1-\varepsilon)|$ is linear in $|\mathbf{S}|$.

nodes.name: Strong variable-setting CE criterion (rewritten)
nodes.statement: $k\geq\min_{x>0}[\phi_\mathcal{O}(x)]^{l_j/j}/x$ for all $j\in E_\mathcal{O}$, where $l_j=\max\{|\mathrm{obj}(\mathfrak{e})|:\mathfrak{e}\in\mathfrak{F}_j\}$.

nodes.name: EC criterion dominates strong CE criterion
nodes.statement: In the independent EC-setting, the entropy-compression criterion (\ref{condentr}) is always at least as strong as the strong variable-setting CE criterion (\ref{opa3}); the two coincide iff all (tidy) flaws of $\mathfrak{F}$ are elementary.
assumptions: Independent EC-setting (all flaws standard, generated by i.i.d. uniform $[k]$-valued variables)
conclusions: Equality iff all events of $\mathfrak{F}$ are elementary (i.e. $l_j=j$ for all $j$)

nodes.name: Non-repetitive vertex coloring
nodes.statement: Apply EC to non-repetitive vertex coloring of a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$: take $\mathbf{S}=V$, $\mathcal{O}=$ all paths of even length, flaw = path is monochromatic. EC criterion yields $k\geq\Delta^2(1+3\cdot 2^{-1/3}\Delta^{-1/3}+o(\Delta^{-1/3}))$.

nodes.name: Star vertex coloring
nodes.statement: EC yields $k\geq 2\sqrt{2}\,\Delta^{3/2}+\Delta$ for the star chromatic index $\pi(G)$, matching the bound of Esperet-Parreau. CE criterion gives $k\geq(8/\sqrt{27})\cdot 2\sqrt{2}\,\Delta^{3/2}+(8/3)\Delta+o(\Delta)$, worse by a factor 1.54.

nodes.name: $\beta$-frugal vertex coloring
nodes.statement: EC criterion gives $\chi_\beta(G)\leq\Delta+\Delta^{1+1/\beta}\beta/[(\beta!)^{1/\beta}(\beta-1)^{1-1/\beta}]$, improving previous bounds. For $\beta=2$ (linear coloring): $\chi_2(G)\leq\sqrt{2}\,\Delta^{3/2}+\Delta$.

nodes.name: Acyclic vertex coloring
nodes.statement: Using objects $\mathcal{O}=P_2\cup C_4\cup S_2\cup P_6$ (paths of length 2, non-special 4-cycles, special pairs, paths of length 6) and the special-pair construction of \cite{AMR}: EC yields $\chi(G)\leq(3/\sqrt[3]{2})\Delta^{4/3}+(7+\sqrt[3]{2})\Delta$. CE criterion yields $k\geq(9/2)\Delta^{4/3}+o(\Delta^{4/3})$, worse by factor 1.89.

nodes.name: Greedy proper edge coloring without bichromatic 4-cycles
nodes.statement: Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ with maximum degree $\Delta$, the edges of $G$ can be colored sequentially using $2\Delta-1$ colors so that the coloring is proper and contains no bichromatic 4-cycle.
conclusions: There exists a sequential proper edge coloring of $G$ using $2\Delta-1$ colors with no bichromatic 4-cycle

nodes.name: Acyclic edge coloring (dependent EC-setting)
nodes.statement: Using non-standard flaws encoding the proper-coloring + 4-cycle avoidance from Lemma 4.1, the EC criterion yields $a'(G)<4(\Delta-1)$, matching the Esperet-Parreau bound. This is the only known dependent EC-setting application.

nodes.name: Independent transversals: EC and CE tie
nodes.statement: For independent transversals of partitioned graphs with $|V_i|\geq k$: $\mathcal{O}$ = connected pairs $\{V_i,V_{i'}\}$, all flaws elementary. EC criterion gives $k_\Delta\leq 4\Delta$, equal to the CE bound (since all flaws are elementary, by Proposition $\ref{compar}$).

nodes.name: Improvement of CELL over LLL via independent sets
nodes.statement: $\Phi_\mathfrak{e}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\mathcal{G})=\sum_{Y\subseteq\Gamma_\mathcal{G}(\mathfrak{e})}\prod_{\mathfrak{e}'\in Y}\mu_{\mathfrak{e}'}\geq\sum_{Y\subseteq\Gamma_\mathcal{G}(\mathfrak{e}),Y\text{ indep}}\prod_{\mathfrak{e}'\in Y}\mu_{\mathfrak{e}'}=\Xi_\mathfrak{e}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\mathcal{G})$, so CELL strictly improves LLL.

nodes.name: Acyclic edge coloring: improvement is mostly due to Lemma 4.1, not EC
nodes.statement: The bound $4(\Delta-1)$ for acyclic edge coloring is much better than the $9.163(\Delta-1)$ obtained earlier via cluster expansion in \cite{NPS}; however the improvement is mainly attributable to Lemma 4.1 (greedy 4-cycle avoidance), not to entropy compression itself. Reapplying CELL after Lemma 4.1 yields $4.181(\Delta-1)$, very close to EC.

nodes.name: Recent improvement (Giotis et al.)
nodes.statement: Giotis, Kirousis, Psaromiligkos, Thilikos \cite{GKPT} improved the bound to $a'(G)\leq 3.79(\Delta-1)$ by combining Lemma 4.1 with a variant of the Moser-Tardos algorithm specific to acyclic edge coloring.
